What this table says for static Eve:
- **Every per-thread structure at this pin is made of allocator blocks at final slab addresses.** Thread-locality is a *naming* property (a wasm global is the only root) plus a *tally* property (allocated quiet or manual, so no scope log notes it). None is a region the thread bump-fills; the only bump allocators in the kernel are BLOCK PAGES (eve.vs:2810–2951, VS-KERNEL.md §2.5) and the link arena (boot.vs:12637–12648, a process that exits).
- **"Scratch" in practice is wider than rule 12's wording.** bnd.vs and the four `$tmemo` tables hold counted values (condition (b) fails as written) and are licensed as "per-thread memos (Q3)" / a per-thread holder; hmemo.vs and the seal reserve (eve.vs:943–968) are the two that meet all four literally. Neither memo family is freed at thread exit (grep above) — condition (d) is met as "never adopted by anything", not as "thrown away".
- **Ownership of an in-place builder is read from the page header** (`PHV2_OWNER` via `page_of`), for both the transient (`tl_owner_is_me`, tally.vs:1236–1237) and the linear conj. A builder working in a region with no owner-stamped page header has no guard to pass or fail by design — it either traps (adopted owner) or is unguarded (owner 0).

## 3.7 The feasibility question: build in a private bump region, then publish in an atom with no copy

Setup: a thread claims one raw region (`claim_region`), bump-fills it with blocks in final ExtCID v3 layout (as `_bp_alloc` does for adopted wire blocks, eve.vs:2914–2951), then wants the root held by an atom. Three ways the region could be dressed decide every answer: **R0** bare (no `PAGE_MAGIC` at its base); **R1** as a BLOCK PAGE — `PAGE_MAGIC`, a CID, one class, `TOTAL_BLOCKS` 0, `BM_OFF` 0, owner `PT_ADOPTED_OWNER`, cursor in `NEXT_FIT` (`_bp_make`, eve.vs:2884–2912); **R2** as an own page (`PAGE_MAGIC`, owner = the thread's id, `TOTAL_BLOCKS` 0).

| subsystem | what it does with such a block (code read unless noted) | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **(a) `free_block_off`** | Order: `tl_forget` (no descriptor → returns), then `region_foreign_p` → 0 refused, then "a block on NO allocator page is not this allocator's to free either — refused (0)" by the magic test (alloc.vs:3351, :3379–3392; tally.vs:1494–1501). **R0**: refused by the magic test — the path a string literal's block and a > 960 KB run take ("which nothing frees"). **R1**: refused by `region_foreign_p` (owner word 2147483646, alloc.vs:1184–1185). **R2**: *not* refused — owner == my id sends it to `free_on_owned_page` → `bitmap_free_in_page_plain`, which computes `block_idx` with **no bound against `TOTAL_BLOCKS`**, loads a "bitmap" word at `page + BM_OFF(0) + …` (the page header itself), may clear a header bit, **stores `word_idx` into `NEXT_FIT` — the bump cursor —** and `fl_push`es the block onto the thread's free list, from which `alloc_block` would hand it out again (alloc.vs:3417–3418, :3647–3676, :3684–3692) | R0/R1: a **leak, by design** ("a false answer could only refuse a free (a leak, never a write into a reused region)", alloc.vs:1167–1168). R2: **corruption** — a bump page must never carry a thread id as owner |
| **(b) the tally** | `tl_desc` answers 0 for all three: no `PAGE_MAGIC` (tally.vs:289); adopted owner (:293–295); `rel >= n * bs` with n = 0 (:316–319). With no descriptor: `tally_hold` returns 0 **before any edge walk** (:1045–1046) — the block is not counted *and its children are not held through it*; `tl_drop_y` 0 (:1083–1084); `tally_count` −1 (:1207); `tally_retire` 0 (:1115); `tally_transient_mark` **traps** — "a block with no descriptor cannot be a transient's" (:1240). `tally_atom_cas` applies the foreign refusal only `(wasm/when (tl_is_block new) …)` (:1721–1723), so such a root is **not refused**: the CAS runs, `tally_hold new` holds nothing, and the atom's slot names an uncounted root (:1729–1735). A counted allocator block may name such a child (`tl_hold_one` → 0: "a permanent block, or no block: nothing to hold", :976–990) | **Storable, never counted, never reclaimed.** The hazard is the other direction: any *allocator* block reachable only through the bump-built root (a boxed scalar, a string, a shared subtree) is held by no one — the scope that allocated it frees it at its toss, or its last other holder's drop does, under the root. The same defect class was measured on `vec_conj_lin`: "Nothing counted them, so the scope that allocated them freed them at its toss under the root … rc 134" (vec.vs:969–979). **Required: closure** — every out-edge of the region lands in memory nothing frees (the region itself, a literal, a PERMANENT block, an adopted page) |
| **(c) seal, slot store, slot resolve** | `seal_block(block_off, payload_size)` reads the block's FLAGS, tag and payload and writes the SHA at `EXTCID_SHA_OFF`; no page lookup of the block (eve.vs:1290–1309). `slot_store` → `_slot_head`: (1) `_slot_room_ok(slot)` reads `PHV2_CLASS_IDX` **at the destination's region base** and traps when it is < class 4 (eve.vs:4069–4070, :4087–4091) — on R0 that word is whatever the region's first block holds at +20; (2) `_eve_page_cid_to(slot, child)`: the child's region CID if its base reads `PAGE` or `EVCT`, **else 16 zero bytes** (eve.vs:1714–1725). `eve_slot_resolve`: a CID-less slot answers `inner` as local, **unless the slot itself lies in an adopted region → −1, the page fault** (eve.vs:3622–3628, `_pt_in_adopted` :3694–3704); a slot with a CID resolves when "the region at INNER_OFFSET carries that CID" (:3642–3647). `_hdr_live(b)` requires INNER_OFFSET = b, or the same in-region offset on an adopted page (eve.vs:2700–2726) — else the block images by reference (tier 4), not by content | Works on R1 (children on the same or another CID-carrying page). On **R0 the slots are CID-less**: fine for local reads from allocator-page parents, a page fault from an adopted-page parent, and **invisible to the page writer** (next row). Blocks must be built at their final address (the own header carries it) |
| **(d) `vs.tier/write-pages`** | Per block: `-page-row` (kernel `alloc_page_info`, `alloc_page_at`: page 0 when the region has no `PAGE_MAGIC`, alloc.vs:2448–2456, :4144–4153) → refuses "a block outside every allocator page" when page = 0, refuses class 15, then reads `rt-class-block-size cls` bytes at the block's address and lays it out by its type-CID (tier.vs:324–330). **No test of the owner word, `TOTAL_BLOCKS` or the bitmap** on the path. But a slot (and the root) whose first 16 bytes are zero is "a slot naming no page (an empty one, a scalar inline)… kept" and **not followed**; a root with a zero CID "is written as nothing: {:root (root-text v) :pages {}}" (tier.vs:314–315, :333–336) | **R1 blocks are accepted** and re-placed into fresh class pages (a copy with address rewrite; "no digest moves", tier.vs:186–189). **R0 blocks are silently dropped from the wire**, not refused. One class per page is assumed (`bs` from the page's class): a mixed-size bump region is misread |
| **(e) eviction / holds** | `eve_region_evict(base)` refuses every region whose owner is not `PT_ADOPTED_OWNER` — "a page of this slab's own allocator is never evicted here" — and a block page that is the class's *current* page in the SHA-table header (eve.vs:2207–2221, :2955–2960). Eviction is one CAS of the magic to `EVCT`; `eve_region_release` then puts the region on the free list; `claim_region_reuse` hands it out once `min_safe − stamp ≥ 2` **and** its hold count is 0 (alloc.vs:945–965). At this pin the only callers of `region_hold_add` are `eve_region_bind` (a compiled form's binding, a closure's captures) and its releases (eve.vs:2364, :2401, :2472; grep `region_hold_add` over vs/src/vs). **The hold a stored value was to get is gone**: eve.vs:2273–2275 and alloc.vs:822 still say "A value an atom, var, def or side table stores is held by the hold ledger (retire.vs rt_lg_region …)", but retire.vs:15–22 lists "the hold ledger (and its QUEUED mark)" among what was "Deleted from this module" and no `rt_lg_*` definition exists (grep `defn-? rt_lg` over vs/src/vs: none; `eve_slot_resolve_held` is defined at eve.vs:3670 and has no caller). The :memory policy takes its candidates from the page table's registered pages, oldest first, and does **not** write a block page back before releasing it (tier.vs:503–549, :547) | **Yes: a registered adopted/block page holding an atom's live state can be evicted and its region reused** once no form binds a value in it (only where a working-set bound is installed — `run-policy!` does nothing without one, tier.vs:554–560). A content page is re-served by its tier on the next fault (residency is a cache); a block page has no tier ("no tier holds a block page", eve.vs:3717–3718; the block tier "is deleted", tier.vs:17–21). Doc/code disagreement recorded. R0/R2 are never evicted |

**Also binding on the builder:** the in-place builders cannot run inside such a region — a transient needs a descriptor (trap, tally.vs:1240) and `vec_conj_lin`'s guard traps on the adopted owner (tally.vs:1262–1265). Kernel-level atom reads take the slot's INNER_OFFSET as the address without resolving the page CID (`tally_atom_value`, `tally_atom_now`, tally.vs:1705–1712, :1742–1757; program_runtime's `kderef` was not read).

### Conclusion

1. **Possible today: no.** No exported entry builds or publishes one. `_bp_alloc` is private to eve.vs, shared (one current page per class, CAS cursor), and reached only from `eve_block_adopt`, `_adopt_slot` and `_bp_box_refault`. The existing kernel checks happen to leave exactly one consistent shape — R1 — and it is a per-class, leak-only, evictable page, not a thread's arena.
2. **Possible with a named small change — only as a PAGE, never as scratch.** The zero-copy precedent is `eve_page_register(base)` for "a region where [the tier] mapped the page itself" (program_runtime.vs:26349–26387; mmap.vs:308–314; VS-KERNEL.md §2.2). The change: let a thread fill a claimed region with a version-5 page image of one class (header + blocks at final in-region offsets, sealed, slots carrying page CIDs) and register it. Conditions the code imposes, all above: one class per region; closure of out-edges; slots written through `slot_store` after the header exists; no transient / linear builder; nothing in it is ever freed singly; and custody for atom-stored values must be restored (a region hold taken at the atom store, or the page must be re-servable by CID from a store) — today's eviction would otherwise reuse it under the atom.
3. **It is an arena by rule 12's own test** the moment it is published: "(b) holds no value and is never reachable from one … (d) is thrown away by its thread when done, never adopted by the allocator's lifetime rules or the tally's walk. Anything that needs the tally, the epoch, or a free list to know about it is an arena and is not built." The page framing is the only one a standing rule already licenses (invariant L: "A wire page is a value page").
4. **A packed (non-block-layout) static value cannot be published without a copy at all**: every reader needs a 256-byte own header at the block's own address (`_hdr_live`), 64-byte slots, and a type-CID at +0.
5. **Existing copy paths, cheapest first (none copies a value into allocator blocks):**

| path | what it costs | where the result lives | where |
|---|---|---|---|
| rebuild through the builders: `vec_create` + `vec_conj_lin` under the deferred seal; transient map | per element: slot store, amortised leaf growth; per node one `alloc_block`; digests once, on demand | **ordinary allocator blocks** (the only path that yields them) | vec.vs:936–1095; eve.vs:1437 — code read |
| `vs.tier/write-pages` → `eve_page_adopt_b64` | a `.vs` walk + per-block text slices + base64 both ways; rewrites INNER_OFFSET and slot heads only, **no re-hash** | an adopted page | tier.vs:301–379; eve.vs:2127–2155 — code read |
| `eve_block_adopt` per block | SHA-256 of the image, expand 32→64-B slots, re-seal (second SHA), canonical check, table insert | a BLOCK PAGE (bump), not an allocator block | eve.vs:3560–3597 (VS-KERNEL.md §2.5) |
| a block-level relocating copier into allocator blocks (`alloc_block` by class, `memory-copy` the extent, rewrite the own INNER_OFFSET and each slot's 24-byte head via `_slot_head`, keep every SHA) | 1 alloc + 1 memcpy + head rewrites per block, no hash | allocator blocks, counted normally | **not found** — grep `clone|copy|relocat` over the kernel: only rb.vs `clone_node` (path copy) and node-local `memory-copy`. The "crossing copies" rule has no copier: the tally refuses (−2) and the runtime traps (tally.vs:1715–1723; program_runtime.vs:3449–3450) |

## 4. The host boundary, and how canonical Eve runs on VS

| question | answer | where / tag |
|---|---|---|
| What is `vs/src/vs/interop.vs`? | **Not a value-to-host converter.** It is "the Java-interop runtime … (the clinj model: WINE, not an emulator)": a class registry held in atoms; "an instance — a map {:vs-type \"<fqcn>\" …fields}; a deftype / defrecord instance's \"<ns>/<T>\" key reads as the class <ns>.<T>"; a method is "a fn registered here under its Java name"; a Class is the value `{:vs-type "java.lang.Class" :name "<fqcn>"}`. No byte leaves the slab through it; `java-str` / `java-hash` answer a registered `toString` / `hashCode` | interop.vs:1–23, :36–43, :697–702 — code read (header + defn index; bodies not read) |
| How does a VS value reach the host, then? | As text: the `vs.host` bridge frames (JSON on fd 1 / fd 0, bytes as base64 or UTF-8) and the two kernel serializers — already in VS-KERNEL.md §4. Nothing further found in interop.vs | VS-KERNEL.md §4 (host.vs:6–21, serial.vs, eve.vs:4299–4513) — first pass |
| Where do canonical Eve's values live on VS? | **In Eve's own slab, not in kernel ExtCID blocks.** "plain functions over the program's own linear memory, read and written with the program-runtime mmap arms — no protocol dispatch, no IMemRegion layer"; a region is "a window of consecutive slab regions no allocator hands out ((mmap/reserve! n)) for a heap region, a file's pages mapped over a fresh window (vs.mmap/map-file!, under vs-eve-host's doorbell) for an mmap region — the same files eve's other hosts map". A slab-qualified offset `[class:3 | block:29]` "is an address in two loads"; the allocator is Eve's (`eve.deftype-proto.alloc`'s `JvmSlabCtx`, slab classes 0–6; "a heap domain holds 7 MB of slab regions") | eve:adapters/slab-io/vs/src/eve/slab_io.vs:1–18, :24–28, :74–76; eve:adapters/region/vs/src/eve/region.vs:2–8 — code read |
| Which memory is that? | The **same** shared wasm linear memory as the kernel's slab, in **foreign runs** (`mmap/reserve!` = `claim_regions` + the 'FRGN' mark, VS-KERNEL.md §1.3): the kernel allocator hands nothing out of them, `free_block_off`, the tally, slot resolution and the page tier all refuse them by `region_in_foreign_run`. "A spike adapter: one thread (the cell is not shared safely)" | eve:adapters/encoding/vs/src/eve/encoding.vs:2–5, :10–13, :28–42; slab_io.vs:89–94; eve:doc/hosts/valuescript.md:55 — code read + doc read |

| a **record** | a MAP root `{:vs-type "<ns>/<T>" <field> v …}` whose meta slot (+332) holds an 'rtyp' box `mkblk 1887007858 3` = `[meta @+24][kind @+28: 1 record · 2 deftype instance][type word @+32]`. "The :vs-type entry stays — `=`, `hash` and a key tell two types apart" | **yes**: the identity is the qualified-name *string* in the map's content (inside its seal), plus the type word | program_runtime.vs:22820–22855 — code read |
| **the type word** | "A type's WORD is eve's (eve/doc/unification/FORMAT-DECISIONS.md §7, eve/src/eve/deftype/registry.cljc): from the type's namespace-qualified name \"ns/T\" through Clojure's `hash` of a string, h — the type-id byte 0x40 + (h mod 173) in bits 0-7 and the name hash h & 0xFFFFFF in bits 8-31 … so every process derives one type's word alike, whatever it loaded and in whatever order." Stored **@+4 of a struct block** (`rt-struct-alloc-t`) and @+32 of a record's 'rtyp' box; `tw_hash` is Murmur3 over Java's `String.hashCode` | **yes — name-derived, 32 bits, name only (fields are not hashed).** No collision check was found (not searched beyond these functions) | program_runtime.vs:85453–85458, :85460–85502, :85524–85529, :85539–85541, :85705–85710 — code read |
| the layout id `:vs-lay-<h>` (first pass, confirmed and corrected) | h = `vs.core/rt-str-hash32` (the same Clojure string hash) of `"<qname>|<f>:<code>|…"` — the qualified name, then each field's name and type code (1 int32 · 2 float64 · 3 boolean · 4 ref) **in declared order**, computed at macro expansion. What the block stores is **not the hash**: "lay is the layout's keyword … an interned keyword, so the block holds its offset" **@+8** | the keyword's *name* is portable; the stored word is a slab address | vs/src/vs/macros.vs:1947–1969; program_runtime.vs:85699–85710, :85719–85725 — code read |
| the struct block's first 16 bytes | word 0 = 0 ("CID word 0 … still 0"), word 1 = the type word, word 2 = the layout keyword's offset; the shape id @+260 is the shape record's slab offset (first pass) | the 16-byte field as bytes: **no** (two process-local addresses around one portable word) | program_runtime.vs:85703–85704; sstruct.vs:20, :44 — code read |
| is a struct content-addressed? | `sstruct.vs` never calls `seal_block` (grep: none; ref fields are written by `slot_store` only), so a parent's slot images a struct by tier 4 — "the REFERENCE IMAGE [type_cid:16][block_off:4][zeros:12]. Deterministic per (type, block); NOT content-addressed" | **no**: a collection holding a fixed-layout deftype instance seals per process (the same consequence eve.vs states for a regex: "images and seals PER OBJECT, by design") | sstruct.vs:30, :267–281; eve.vs:3998–4008 — code read |

Answer: **a portable, name-derived type identity exists, and it is Eve's own 32-bit type word** — but no 16-byte type-CID is derived for any user type (VS-KERNEL.md §5: the kernel's CIDs are pinned placeholders), field layout is identified only by a keyword whose in-block form is an address, and fixed-layout instances are identity values outside content addressing.

## 6. Where Eve went in atom.broker

- **No `eve/` tree**: `ls -d eve eve.atom` → "No such file or directory" (ran). The pin's own subject: "Land the Eve extraction: eve/ subtree removed; Eve lives in SeniorCareMarket/eve and atom.broker consumes it as a dep pin (0.9.3.1)" (`git log -1`, ran). DECLARATION.md: "the `eve/` subtree is deleted from the branch, last, after the proofs" (docs/eve-extraction/DECLARATION.md:42–43 — doc read).
- **The dep is the release tree, not the old subtree**: "monorepo `main`'s `eve/`: 2,307 files; the dep tree: 824 files. 495 files identical, 125 differing, 204 only in the dep, 1,687 only in the subtree"; the dep adds `src/eve/stm.cljc`, the DataScript port, the jank adapters (docs/eve-extraction/EXTRACTION-MAP.md:36–52 — doc read).
- **VS's vendoring is a procedure, not a file**: "There is no vendor script and no committed vendored copy on `main`" — the copy is made from the dep checkout and sha256-walked; "VS compiles Eve from roots = the vendored tree's `src` + its `hosts.edn` `:vs` adapter roots" (EXTRACTION-MAP.md:125–140 — doc read).

## Kill/support evidence

### A8 — "a packed 64 KiB chunk can live in an allocator page next to ordinary blocks without the hand-off being a copy anyway" — **killed as worded; a narrower form survives**

- **Kill 1 — not next to ordinary blocks.** No bitmap class holds it (largest 10,240 B, alloc.vs:548–549). Its only allocator home is one class-15 block on a coalescing page: ≤ 15 per region, 4-byte aligned, among other > 10 KB blocks such as big strings and the per-thread memo tables of §3.6 (VS-KERNEL.md §1.3, §1.6).
- **Kill 2 — the allocator picks the address.** No entry takes a placement (VS-KERNEL.md §1.7), so a chunk that already exists anywhere else arrives by `memory.copy`. The hand-off is copy-free only when the producer writes into the block it was handed — "Caller gets back a block offset in $data and writes fields directly at that offset — no stage-then-commit pattern" (alloc.vs:3–5); the precedents are raw bytes: the base64 decode "straight into a freshly claimed region" (eve.vs:2122) and the slurp "read straight into a `leaf_big`'s payload" (row 8 above).
- **Kill 3 — nothing inside it is a block.** `tl_desc` finds a class-15 descriptor only "at v's exact data offset" (tally.vs:305–312), so an interior address is uncounted and unfreeable; `_hdr_live` wants INNER_OFFSET = the block's own address (eve.vs:2710–2726); the tally's edge walk dispatches per known kind on the bytes at +0 and counts any other shape as unknown, with no edges (tally.vs:732–880, :838). A packed chunk is a **leaf**: it may not be the only path to an allocator block (§3.7 (b)).
- **Kill 4 — it cannot go on the wire as pages.** "a block of the coalescing class (15) is past the page writer's classes" (tier.vs:326–327); and a parent's slot images an unknown flat kind by reference, per process (eve.vs:4003–4008, :4101–4106).
- **Support — the survivor.** One chunk as one opaque class-15 block the tally counts and frees as a unit: class-15 descriptors carry COUNT, FLAGS and EPOCH (alloc.vs:300–315), a foreign free queues, a free merges neighbours (alloc.vs:3399–3415). That is one big flat value block produced in place — not a chunk of blocks, and not adjacent to the value's other blocks.

### A9 — "the allocator can consume pre-mapped placement" — **killed for the allocator; true only of the page tier, which keeps the bytes out of the allocator for good**

- **Kill.** alloc.vs takes memory in exactly three ways — `claim_region`, `claim_regions`, `claim_region_reuse` — plus orphan adoption of pages it minted itself; nothing accepts an address, a filled range or a page image (VS-KERNEL.md §1.4, §1.7).
- **Where placement *is* consumed.** `eve_page_register(base)` for a region the host mapped (zero-copy with `vs.mmap/map-value-page!`) and `eve_page_adopt_b64` (VS-KERNEL.md §2.2). The result is never the allocator's: "the allocator's walks … hand nothing out of it and no thread adopts it as an orphan" (eve.vs:1986–1988); frees refused (alloc.vs:3380–3382); blocks uncounted (tally.vs:293–295); transients and the linear conj trap on it (tally.vs:1240, :1262–1265); evictable (§3.7 (e)).
- **Support — how near a wire page is to an allocator page.** `write-pages` emits a well-formed version-5 page of one class: header, an all-ones bitmap for its n blocks, zero-filled descriptor columns, `TOTAL_BLOCKS` = n, the data offset computed for n (tier.vs:269–271, :287–291, :366–372). Making it an owned page needs an owner hand-off (`PT_ADOPTED_OWNER` → a thread id, plus that thread's directory entry), localising each headed block's INNER_OFFSET (`_hdr_live` accepts a foreign offset only on an adopted region, eve.vs:2712–2721) and a hold walk to establish n counts. No payload byte moves; it is still per-block work, no code does it, and the page it yields has no free block. The rule in its way: "A count never lives on a remotely-owned page: cross-domain bare references do not exist (a foreign value is refused at `swap!`; a crossing copies)" (vs/docs/contention-domains.md:205–207, quoted in VS-KERNEL.md §0).

### O10 — what the kernel would need so thread-local, off-allocator, ephemeral construction can be fed to the allocator fast

| # | option | kernel change | what it buys | standing rule it touches (verbatim) |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | stay in the allocator: transients, the linear conj, the per-form scope (the incumbent) | none | blocks are born at their final addresses — "Promotion is a STORE by the adopter (tally_atom_cas): no copy, no forward table" (tally.vs:1820) | none; it is the ruling: "Let's fix the transients and go with that for local state." (L22-eve-kernel.md:614–615) |
| 2 | a **run entry** in alloc.vs: n consecutive blocks of one class on an owned page in one call (a freshly minted owned sub-page is all clear; the owner sets bits with plain stores, alloc.vs:2118–2188) | small and additive: alloc.vs, plus the log hook at alloc.vs:1999–2001 noting a run | a decoder lays blocks by pointer bump **inside allocator memory**; every guard, count, free, seal and the page writer hold unchanged; planning per run, not per block; one cursor per class | none of rule 12's prohibitions — nothing is held aside, free state stays in the bitmap, the builder initialises. Cost is process: a kernel change is a landing ("about 18 min with a kernel change", CLAUDE.md) |
| 3 | thread scratch + a **relocating copier** into allocator blocks (memcpy, own INNER_OFFSET, slot heads; SHAs kept) | one new kernel routine (§3.7, last table row) | one copy, no hashing, no content re-planning | the carve-out, which it meets only while nothing in the scratch is published: "(b) holds no value and is never reachable from one — no reader, no slot, no count names it; … (d) is thrown away by its thread when done" |
| 4 | a per-thread **bump page published as a page** (§3.7 R1) | a thread-private `_bp_alloc`, a region hold for atom-stored roots (the deleted ledger), a closure check | no copy | "No arenas. No scratch buffers. Both are forms of 'hold memory aside and reuse the bytes' that fight the forget model." · "Anything that needs the tally, the epoch, or a free list to know about it is an arena and is not built." · the nursery determination (§7 rows 1–2) |
| 5 | owner hand-off of an adopted page (A9's support) | owner CAS, INNER_OFFSET localisation, count walk | no payload byte moves | "Storing a foreign value into an atom copies it in. There are no foreign references inside an atom — its tree is wholly its own." (vs/docs/contention-domains.md:26–27) |
| 6 | a packed chunk as one class-15 leaf (A8's survivor) | a flat-kind arm in `_slot_flat_kind` for content addressing; a tally edge arm if it may hold references | a compact payload under the tally's custody | rule 26: "A JSON blob, a sidecar map, a value envelope, a side record standing in for a header field: none of these is built"; invariant J licenses flat blocks for scalars ("collections hold blocks, never values") |

Reading of the table: option 2 is the only one in which the ephemeral blocks and the persistent blocks are the same blocks and no standing rule is touched. Options 4–6 each need an operator ruling, and option 4 re-opens a question the operator answered on 2026-10-18. Not measured anywhere in the files read: the per-call cost of `alloc_block`, and the cost of a block-level copy against a rebuild — both are needed before choosing between options 1, 2 and 3.
